subject: platform/marketing
professional: a technical SEO / search-distribution engineer who runs IndexNow submissions for a large site (checks first: payload matches the indexnow.org spec, every URL is on the declared host and under the keyLocation path, the key file is reachable and equals the key, request size limits, honest handling of 200/202/422/429)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against the indexnow.org protocol (JSON POST {host,key,keyLocation,urlList}; key 8-128 chars [a-zA-Z0-9-]; key file body equals key; max 10,000 URLs per request; Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8). (1) Ran buildPayload({baseUrl:'https://a.test/p/',urls:[...]}) and got host a.test, keyLocation https://a.test/p/<key>.txt, key 51c80c301d4b5583163e00e6c89b06cf (32 hex, valid), exactly the spec shape. (2) Built a fixture site in the scratchpad (catalog.json with 4 URLs, sitemap index with 3 children, one missing, one foreign host) and ran node indexnow.mjs --dir <fixture>: hand count 4 catalog + 2 valid sitemap locs, 1 duplicate (t1/) = 6 unique, tool printed 6; the & in a sitemap loc was unescaped to & as the XML spec requires; the missing and foreign children were warned and skipped. (3) isEgressRefusal: 403+'Host not in allowlist' true, 403+'Forbidden key' false, 429+allowlist text false, which matches the stated intent that IndexNow's own 403 (invalid key) stays loud. (4) fetchHint('origin/gh-pages') gives 'git fetch origin gh-pages', which git accepts. Never sent a network request. Counter-finding: a URL inside a valid child sitemap that is on another host or outside the keyLocation path is submitted unfiltered (fixture: https://evil.test/x/ and https://example.test/outside/ both appeared in the list); the spec says all URLs must be on the host and, for a subpath key, under it, otherwise the request is rejected. Not scored 4 because of that.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: dry-run default (works, exit 0, sends nothing); --ref and --dir readers (--dir works; --ref gh-pages fails here only because the ref is not fetched, with the documented hint); --base-url explicit override (works, rejects ftp:// and non-URLs); sitemap-index walk one level with warnings (works); union with catalog floor (works); key-file check before submit (assertKeyFilePublished, covered by tests); EXIT_NO_EGRESS 3 (covered by tests; not run live by design); empty list and >10000 guards (tested). README also claims publish-branch.sh and a workflow call it and indexnow_state.py reports status; those are outside this directory and were not exercised. No stubs or TODOs found. Not batching above 10,000 URLs is a stated, loud limit.
evidence.verification: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs' in platform/marketing: 38 tests, 38 pass, 0 fail, ~2.3 s. Seeded mutations, each reverted with git checkout: (a) MAX_URLS_PER_REQUEST 10000 to 10001 plus isEgressRefusal early-return false to true: 2 tests failed (#6 ceiling, #20 IndexNow's own 403 stays a real failure). (b) removed the & unescape in locsIn: test #7 failed. (c) disabled the child-sitemap baseUrl guard (if (false)): tests #11 and #17 failed. All 3 mutations caught. Gap: no test asserts that sitemap URLs on a foreign host are filtered, because the code does not do it (defect below); the main CLI block (~100 lines) is exercised only through subprocess tests.
evidence.craft: Read all of indexnow.mjs (619 lines) and the test file's structure. Strengths: pure exported functions, injected reader, narrow error matching, fail-closed on origin conflict, tests per function. Defects: (1) unhandled throws print raw Node stack traces for user errors: missing ref (fatal: invalid object name 'gh-pages' with a stack), --base-url ftp://x or 'notaurl', and a trailing '--ref' with no value silently becomes undefined and falls through to a dry run on the wrong input; (2) parseArgs silently ignores unknown flags (a typo like --sumbit leaves a dry run with no warning); (3) the summary line 'N from K published sitemap(s)' uses childCount of named children, not those actually read, so it said '3 from 3' when only 1 was read; (4) ~190 lines of comment prose with dated incident narrative and stale counts (881/973/261/252) embedded in doc blocks, and a doc-comment for readerFor is stacked above fetchHint's, so readerFor has none; (5) error text still points at 'the Hetzner box once host mode is installed' and gitops/prod/host/refresh-site.sh, both retired 2026-10-01/30; (6) knownRemotes shells out to git on every fetchHint call.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: dry-run default (code, tests), key mismatch refusal (assertKeyFilePublished + test), narrow egress match (isEgressRefusal + tests), 10,000 ceiling (matches indexnow.org), 'there is no Google equivalent' and 'asked, not done' caveat (correct, stated). Unbacked or stale: README says 881 published pages, 399 products with null visitors, and the code comments cite 973/979/261/252 as current; none are re-derived in this directory and they disagree with each other. README and the CLI's no-egress message cite the retired Hetzner box as a destination, and the header comment cites https://marisstella.dev refresh-site.sh in gitops/ which was deleted 2026-10-30 (README itself says so in its intro, contradicting resolveBaseUrl's docstring). README says publish-branch.sh 'now calls this itself' and the workflow carries a complement step; not verified here. No disclaimer needed (no user-facing page).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: an operator wants to announce the whole published site to Bing/Yandex/Naver/Seznam. Dry run on a realistic fixture works and shows origin, host, keyLocation and count; the key-file guard prevents a bad submission. Cannot be completed from an agent sandbox (no egress; honest exit 3) so the live path was not exercised; the only real submission route depends on a CI step. Gaps a practitioner would hit in the first hour: no URL-host/path filtering (one stray URL gets the whole 970-URL request rejected with 422), no batching above 10,000, no handling or reporting of 202 vs 200 vs 422 vs 429 beyond ok/not ok, no persisted record of what was submitted (acknowledged in the README), and no incremental mode (resubmits everything every time, which IndexNow guidance discourages for unchanged URLs).
evidence.domain: Compared with the indexnow.org documentation: payload shape, key format, key file location via keyLocation, 10,000-URL cap and POST headers all conform. Departures: no check that urlList entries share host and sit under the keyLocation directory (spec requirement); no use of the 'only changed URLs' guidance (submits the full catalogue each run); no distinction of 200/202/400/403/422/429 in output. The decision to take URLs from published sitemaps rather than the build is sound practice for an SEO engineer. A senior practitioner would sign it off for a single-site announcer with those limits stated.

defects.what: URLs read from child sitemaps are not filtered to the declared host or the keyLocation path, so one foreign or out-of-path <loc> is submitted and the IndexNow spec says the request is then rejected (422) as a whole; reproduced in a dry run with a fixture (evil.test and /outside/ both included)
Full catalogue is resubmitted on every run with no changed-URL mode and no distinction of 200/202/422/429 responses; the stated 'announced' state is only 'asked'
User errors (missing git ref, invalid --base-url) surface as raw stack traces; unknown flags and a valueless --ref are silently accepted so a typo like --sumbit gives a dry run
Summary line reports the number of named child sitemaps as the number read ('3 from 3' when 2 were skipped)
Stale text: retired Hetzner/gitops host named as a destination and caller, and page counts (881/973/979/261) that disagree with one another; readerFor's doc block is displaced by fetchHint's

verdict: A small, careful, well-tested IndexNow submitter: 38/38 tests pass, three seeded mutations in core logic were each caught, the payload and key handling match the indexnow.org spec, and the offline dry run on a fixture produced the hand-computed URL set, origin, host and keyLocation. It does not meet the bar because of claims: the README and comments carry stale and mutually inconsistent page counts and still name the retired Hetzner host as a destination. The worst functional defect is that URLs from child sitemaps are not filtered to the declared host and keyLocation path, so a single stray entry would make the real submission fail as a whole, a case no test covers. Finished (completeness 3) but not at the bar. Live submission was not exercised (no egress).
